svg.title: Climb performance: what reduces the climb
svg.desc: Maximum angle of climb at VX gains the most height for the least ground distance; maximum rate of climb at VY gains the most height in time. PHAK example: in 30 seconds an airplane reaches 1,000 feet AGL over 3,000 feet of ground at VX, or 1,500 feet over 6,000 feet at VY. More weight, higher altitude, gear down and flaps down all reduce excess thrust and excess power, so both maximum climb angle and rate fall. Rate of climb is zero at the absolute ceiling; the service ceiling is where the climb is 100 feet per minute or less.
svg.text: Climb performance: what reduces the climb
Climbing is work, so climb performance depends on excess thrust (angle of climb) or excess power (rate
of climb). Anything that eats the excess hurts both.
VX: 1,000 ft AGL after 30 s
3,000 ft over the ground
VY: 1,500 ft after 30 s
6,000 ft over the ground
Same airplane, 30 seconds of climb at maximum throttle (PHAK example, schematic)
Maximum angle of climb (VX): most altitude for the
least ground covered. Use it to clear trees or
power lines after a short-field takeoff.
Maximum rate of climb (VY): the most altitude in a
given time. It may not be enough to clear an obstacle
that VX would clear.
Four things that lower both maximum angle and maximum rate of climb
More weight
Higher altitude
Landing gear down
Flaps down
Each one reduces both excess thrust and excess power
Excess power is what climbs
130 hp level flight
70 hp
Engine makes 200 hp at this altitude (PHAK example)
Weight: more weight needs a higher angle of
attack, so more induced and parasite drag, so less
reserve thrust for climbing
More weight also lowers the maximum rate of climb,
and it must be flown at a higher climb speed
Altitude and the ceilings
Altitude
Rate of climb
Absolute ceiling: zero rate of climb
Service ceiling: cannot climb faster
than 100 fpm
sea level rate
Climb performance diminishes with altitude
The speeds for best angle, best rate and level
flight converge at the absolute ceiling: no excess
power, one speed holds level flight
